Lina: Heads-up — hit a weird bundler/runtime mismatch while trying to use the JS SDK in an edge SSR app. Different symptom from the usual default/import thing.
Marco: ok what happened?
Lina: When bundling with webpack/vite/rollup the SDK ends up resolved to the CJS file even though package.json has conditional exports. On Node it works; on Vercel Edge it throws `ReferenceError: require is not defined`.
Harper: That sounds like the bundler picked the `require` target (cjs) for the bundle output, then the edge runtime ran an ESM bundle and `require` wasn't available. Can you paste a minimal repro?
Lina: Minimal steps:
```
# repo: https://example.com/rw-repro-mainfield.git
git clone https://example.com/rw-repro-mainfield.git
cd rw-repro-mainfield
npm ci
# build with each bundler
npm run build:vite
npm run build:rollup
npm run build:webpack
# serve the bundle on a local ESM-only runner or deploy to Vercel Edge
```
Lina: Key files: package.json has "type": "module" in the app and the SDK pkg uses exports: {".": {"import":"dist/index.mjs","require":"dist/index.cjs"}}.
Marco: Which bundler configs? mainFields / resolve order matter here.
Lina: Vite default uses rollup resolve which prefers `module`/`jsnext:main` fields; however if your package has a `main` field or the bundler's mainFields ordering includes `main` before `module`, rollup might pick CJS. For webpack, `resolve.mainFields` defaults to [`browser`, `module`, `main`] in dev but can change for target=web or module output. In our repro, webpack ended up resolving to `dist/index.cjs` because our rollup-plugin-node-resolve fallback resolved `main` first in one config.
Nate: Do you have the actual resolved import map from the build? That helps.
Lina: From the Vite build log (trimmed):
```
[plugin:node-resolve] preferring 'main' for redwood-inference -> /node_modules/redwood-inference/dist/index.cjs
```
Lina: Bundle runtime error (Edge): `ReferenceError: require is not defined` at vendor.js:12345
Harper: Another gotcha: TypeScript's `package.json` exports + `types: "dist/index.d.ts"` aren't consulted by bundlers; they use resolution algorithm. Also if your app tsconfig has `module: 'esnext'` but bundler transforms, resolution can pick the wrong entry.
Marco: Quick workaround: force the bundler to prefer `module`/`import` entry. Examples:
- webpack: resolve.mainFields = ['module','main'] or set `resolve.conditionNames` to include 'import'
- rollup/vite: pass `resolve.mainFields: ['module','main']` to @rollup/plugin-node-resolve
Lina: In the repro I added a rollup config patch: `nodeResolve({ mainFields: ['module', 'main'] })` and Vite `resolve: { mainFields: ['module', 'main'] }` — that fixed picking the ESM build and edge runtime worked.
Nate: Longer term SDK fixes: expose a browser import condition, e.g. "exports": { ".": { "browser": "dist/index.browser.mjs", "import": "dist/index.mjs", "require": "dist/index.cjs" } } so bundlers targeting browsers/edges prefer the browser key. Also ensure package.json has `module` and `browser` fields to help older bundlers.
Harper: Another issue: some bundlers treat files with .cjs differently even when imports point to .mjs. Also `sideEffects: false` in the SDK can cause the runtime entry to be tree-shaken if top-level only-type imports exist in consumer code. Any chance sideEffects is set?
Lina: The SDK has `sideEffects: false` in package.json. In the repro I removed it and the symptom changed (the whole package got dropped in some configurations). So we should be careful.
Marco: Action items:
1) Add a dedicated `browser`/`exports.browser` target in the SDK package so bundlers for web/edge pick ESM browser build.
2) Add docs for consumers: config snippets for webpack/vite/rollup to force ESM entry.
3) Add CI bundle-tests that run a tiny app with each bundler and assert the built bundle doesn't call `require`. (Harper: can we add a tiny Node ESM runner?)
Harper: Yep. I'll add a GH Action that runs `npm run build:{vite,rollup,webpack}` and then `node --input-type=module` to execute a small bundle. Fails if `require is not defined` or if runtime throws.
build-bot: CI job bundle-check failed on branch fix/export-browser: https://ci.example.com/runs/5678 — error `ReferenceError: require is not defined`
Nate: For immediate user-facing guidance, add a troubleshooting note in SDK README: "If you see require is not defined in edge runtimes, add `resolve.mainFields: ['module','main']` (webpack/vite/rollup) or upgrade to bundler that respects `exports.browser`."
Lina: I'll open an SDK issue with the repro and propose adding `exports.browser` + small ESM browser build and a tiny changelog note about `sideEffects`. Assigning @eng-devex and @pkg-maintainers.
Harper: Also let's add a short sample app in examples/edge that uses Vite + templates that are validated in CI. That will catch regressions early.
Marco: Cool. Tag me on the PR and I'll review the packaging changes.
Lina: Thanks — posting the issue/PR links here when created. :rocket
